question: Confirm or refute the reported names of rva 0x678B70 SaveWriteInt, 0x678D40 SaveWriteBool and 0x678FB0 SaveWriteString, and establish the shape of CSaveWriter and how a nested object gets written.

addresses.name: SaveWriteFixed
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteFixed(SaveToken key@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@EDI, int thousandths@stack:4)
addresses.comment: **Not SaveWriteInt.** Writes `<key>=<n>.<nnn>` and a newline for a value the game holds in thousandths: SaveWriteKey, then a CToken, then SaveWriteToken(tok_newline). In a text save it hands the int to MakeFixedToken, which formats it `%d.%03d` as tok_fixed (0xD); in a binary save (writer->binary set) it formats the raw int `%d` as tok_int (0xC) instead, so no precision is lost either way. The writer arrives in EDI, not ESI as in the plain-int sibling at 0x678CA0 - the compiler picked a register per function, so the call sites decide.
addresses.evidence: Body at VA 0xA78B70 (image.both: 0x00A78B70, rva 0x678B70) calls SaveWriteKey(0xA7A1B0) with ECX untouched, then either MakeFixedToken(0xA694C0, `%d.%03d`, type 0xD) or _snprintf with '%d' at 0x15DC2B4 and type 0xC, then SaveWriteValue(0xA797A0) and SaveWriteToken(0x461360) with ECX=0x10 tok_newline; `ret 4` against one stack argument. The branch is `cmp byte [edi+0xC],0 / je` and CSaveWriter+0xC is `binary`, so the `%d.%03d` arm is the *text* arm. Call sites in CProvince::SaveContents (rva 0x95020) push the value and set ECX=key, EDI=writer at 0x4952E4 (0x1EA manpower), 0x495307 (0x49B leadership) and 0x49532A (0x207 revolt_risk). A real text save agrees: autosave.hoi3 has `manpower=0.100`, `leadership=0.100`, `revolt_risk=9.000`, while `points=0` and `out_of_supply_days=2109` - the two the province writes through SaveWriteValue by hand - are bare integers. What would show it wrong: a text save writing one of those three keys as a bare integer, or a call site that sets ESI rather than EDI before the call.

addresses.name: SaveWriteBool
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteBool(SaveToken key@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@ESI, bool value@stack:4)
addresses.comment: Writes `<key>=yes` or `<key>=no` and a newline. SaveWriteKey, then a tok_bool (0xE) CToken whose text is `%s` of the literal `yes` at VA 0x15C1914 or `no` at 0x15C1918, then SaveWriteToken(tok_newline). There is no binary branch: the word goes out as a tok_bool either way, and it is SaveWriteValue that decides how a tok_bool is encoded.
addresses.evidence: Body at VA 0xA78D40 (rva 0x678D40): `cmp byte [ebp+8],0` picks between the two literals, sets the CToken type word to 0xE, and calls SaveWriteValue then SaveWriteToken(0x10); `ret 4` against one stack argument, ESI never restored so it is an incoming register. CProvince::SaveContents at 0x4952C8 does `push eax / mov ecx,0x1F9 (capital) / mov esi,ebx / call`, and the province writes `capital` only when the byte at +0x2B0 is true. Strings read straight out of the image: 0x15C1914 = 'yes', 0x15C1918 = 'no'. What would show it wrong: a call site that leaves ESI alone, or a text save writing a boolean key as 1/0.

addresses.name: SaveWriteString
addresses.comment: Writes a **quoted string value and a newline - it writes no key**, so the caller does SaveWriteKey first and this is the right half of `owner="NOR"`. In a text save it builds `"` + the string + `"` with std::string::operatorPlus and the one-character literal at VA 0x15E14F8, formats it `%s` into a tok_word (0xF) CToken and calls SaveWriteValue; in a binary save it copies the string unquoted into the same tok_word and writes that. Then SaveWriteToken(tok_newline) on both paths. The most-called member of the family: 281 direct calls.
addresses.evidence: Body at VA 0xA78FB0 (rva 0x678FB0): ECX is copied to ESI and used as the std::string, [ebp+8] is the writer and is the operand of `cmp byte [eax+0xC],bl`; the CToken's type word is set to 0xF from EDI (`lea edi,[ebx+0xF]`), SaveWriteValue is called at 0xA79098/0xA7918E and SaveWriteToken(ECX=0x10) at 0xA791C3; `ret 4`. It contains no call to SaveWriteKey (0xA7A1B0), and every call site pairs it with one - CProvince::SaveContents at 0x4950C5/0x4950CF (0x1EC owner), 0x495145/0x49514F (0x1ED controller), 0x4951C5/0x4951CF (0x784 underground_owner), 0x495287/0x495291 (0x201 core), 0x495355/0x49535E (0x5C5 strategic_resource), 0x495746/0x49574E (0x591 last_convoy_attack); at 0x4950CA the caller pushes the writer and puts the Hoi3CString it just built with std::string::assign in ECX. autosave.hoi3 shows exactly those keys quoted: `owner="NOR"`, `controller="GER"`, `core="NOR"`. What would show it wrong: a call site that does not call SaveWriteKey first, or a save with an unquoted owner.

addresses.name: SaveWriteInt
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteInt(SaveToken key@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@ESI, int value@stack:4)
addresses.comment: The real `<key>=<int>` writer, and the sibling 0x678B70 was mistaken for: SaveWriteKey, a tok_int (0xC) CToken formatted `%d`, SaveWriteValue, SaveWriteToken(tok_newline). No binary branch - an integer is an integer in both formats. Only four call sites, because most integer keys are written by hand as SaveWriteKey + SaveWriteValue inside the SaveContents itself.
addresses.evidence: Body at VA 0xA78CA0 (rva 0x678CA0): `push esi / call SaveWriteKey` with ECX untouched, `_snprintf(buf,0xFF,'%d',[ebp+8])` into a CToken whose type word is 0xC, SaveWriteValue, SaveWriteToken(0x10); `ret 4`, ESI never restored. Caller at VA 0x5EEB70 does `push [eax+0x10] / mov ecx,0x1F9 / mov esi,[ebp+8] / call`. What would show it wrong: a caller that sets EDI instead of ESI, or one that writes its own key beforehand.

addresses.name: SaveWriteUInt
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteUInt(SaveToken key@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@ESI, unsigned int value@stack:4)
addresses.comment: SaveWriteInt's unsigned twin: identical body but `%u` at VA 0x15FD128 and the CToken type word tok_uint (0x14) rather than tok_int (0xC). One call site in the image.
addresses.evidence: Body at VA 0xA78CF0 (rva 0x678CF0) differs from 0xA78CA0 only in the format pointer (0x15FD128 = '%u') and the type constant (0x14); `ret 4`. Its one caller at VA 0x5F0207 sets ECX from a lookup's return value, ESI from [ebp+8] and pushes the value. What would show it wrong: the string at 0x15FD128 not being '%u', or SaveToken 0x14 not being tok_uint.

addresses.name: SaveWriteKeyString
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteKeyString(SaveToken key@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@ESI, Hoi3CString* value@stack:4)
addresses.comment: The two halves of `<key>="<text>"` in one call: SaveWriteKey followed by SaveWriteString. Seventeen call sites; everywhere else the SaveContents calls the two separately because it has to build the string first.
addresses.evidence: Body at VA 0xA79210 (rva 0x679210) is six instructions: `push esi / call 0xA7A1B0 / mov ecx,[ebp+8] / push esi / call 0xA78FB0 / ret 4`. Caller at VA 0x5EF2C0 does `push this+0x10 / mov ecx,0x37D / mov esi,[ebp+8] / call`. What would show it wrong: the callee at 0xA78FB0 turning out to write a key of its own, which would double it.

addresses.name: SaveWriteKeyToken
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteKeyToken(SaveToken key@ECX, CSaveWriter* writer@ESI, SaveToken value@stack:4)
addresses.comment: Writes `<key>=<word>` where the value is itself a save token written by its own text - an enum member spelled out, the way `automate_trade=yes` or a named mode is. SaveWriteKey, SaveWriteToken(value), SaveWriteToken(tok_newline).
addresses.evidence: Body at VA 0xA791E0 (rva 0x6791E0): `push esi / call 0xA7A1B0 / mov ecx,[ebp+8] / push esi / call 0x461360 / push esi / mov ecx,0x10 / call 0x461360 / ret 4`, where 0x461360 is the recorded SaveWriteToken and 0x10 is tok_newline. Caller at VA 0x5EEE14 puts a token id returned by 0x4C83E0 on the stack, 0x216 in ECX and the writer in ESI. What would show it wrong: a call site passing something other than a token id as the stack argument.

addresses.name: SaveWriteNamedFixed
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteNamedFixed(Hoi3CString* key@EAX, CSaveWriter* writer@EDI, int thousandths@stack:4)
addresses.comment: SaveWriteFixed for a key that is not a token: the key is a runtime string, so it open-codes what SaveWriteKey does - indent by depth-1, write the name as a tok_word, write tok_equals - and then writes the value exactly as SaveWriteFixed does, `%d.%03d` as tok_fixed in a text save and `%d` as tok_int in a binary one, followed by a newline. This is how a save writes rows keyed by a moddable name rather than by a built-in token.
addresses.evidence: Body at VA 0xA78BE0 (rva 0x678BE0): EAX is copied to ESI and read as an Hoi3CString (`cmp [esi+0x14],0x10` is the small-string test against Hoi3CString::maxLength), formatted `%s` into a tok_word (0xF) CToken, SaveWriteValue, SaveWriteToken(ECX=1 tok_equals); the value half is byte-identical in shape to 0xA78B70, calling MakeFixedToken at 0xA694C0 on the text path; `ret 4`. The indent prologue `cmp byte [edi+0xC],0 / mov eax,[edi+4] / test / dec / SaveWriteIndent` is the same code CPersistent::Save and SaveWriteKey use, which is what fixes EDI as the writer. Caller at VA 0x474745 sets EAX to a string reached through two pointers and EDI from [ebp+8] at 0x474721. What would show it wrong: a call site that puts the writer in ESI, or one whose EAX is not a string.

addresses.name: MakeFixedToken
addresses.comment: Builds a tok_fixed (0xD) CToken in the caller's buffer from a thousandths integer: divides by 1000, formats `%d.%03d`, and handles a value between -999 and 0 by writing the sign separately (`-%d.%03d` at VA 0x15FD138) so that -1 comes out `-0.001` rather than `0.-001`. This is the one place the game's thousandths convention becomes text. Returns the buffer in EAX.
addresses.evidence: Body at VA 0xA694C0 (rva 0x6694C0): `mov dword [esi],0xD` then the signed magic-number divide by 0x3E8 (multiplier 0x10624DD3, `sar edx,6`), then _snprintf into esi+4 with '%d.%03d' at 0x15FD144 or '-%d.%03d' at 0x15FD138; every path ends `mov eax,esi / ret` - a bare ret with no stack arguments. Its callers 0xA78B70 and 0xA78BE0 set EAX to the address of the value and ESI to a 0x104-byte stack buffer whose layout matches the recorded CToken (type at +0, text at +4). SaveToken 0xD is tok_fixed. What would show it wrong: the text in a save not matching `%d.%03d` for a field written through it - autosave.hoi3's `revolt_risk=9.000` and `manpower=0.100` say it does.

struct_fields.name: type
struct_fields.revises: the writer family pins the numeric token types the old comment only half-listed: 0xC is tok_int and 0x14 is tok_uint, where the comment called 0x14 'an integer' and did not mention 0xC, 0xD or 0xE at all
struct_fields.comment: the token's kind, itself a token id: 1 `=`, 3 `{`, 4 `}`, 0x10 a newline, 0x11 a tab, 0x12 a space, 0x13 the end of input, and on the write side 0xC tok_int, 0xD tok_fixed (`%d.%03d`, a thousandths value), 0xE tok_bool (`yes`/`no`), 0xF tok_word (a name, and a quoted string), 0x14 tok_uint, 0x18F long_float. In a binary save this is what gets written, as two bytes, and tok_newline, tok_tab and 0x12 are dropped instead.
struct_fields.evidence: Each constant is the literal the writer stores into the type word immediately before calling SaveWriteValue: 0xC at VA 0xA78C08 and 0xA78CBF, 0xD at 0xA694C0 and 0xA78EE2, 0xE at 0xA78D53, 0xF at 0xA78C08's string arm and 0xA79064, 0x14 at 0xA78D0F; the names come from the SaveToken enum already in the findings (tok_int=0xC, tok_fixed=0xD, tok_bool=0xE, tok_word=0xF, tok_uint=0x14). SaveWriteValue's binary arm at 0xA79AB6 compares the type against 0x12, 0x10 and 0x11 and returns without writing for all three. What would show it wrong: a writer storing one of those constants and producing text of a different shape.

slots_noted: none of the nine bodies is in any class's virtual table - vtable.py --holding reports 'is in no class's virtual table' for each of 0xA78B70, 0xA78D40, 0xA78FB0, 0xA78CA0, 0xA78CF0, 0xA79210, 0xA791E0, 0xA78BE0 and 0xA694C0. They are free functions the SaveContents bodies call directly.
frontier_note: 0x7960AF and 0x799AF0 are the CRT formatters every writer ends in - image.functionStart for the call targets 0x79625D (a vsnprintf-style sprintf) and 0x79A1AD (_snprintf). 0x679D40 writes one CToken a given number of times and is what SaveWriteIndent calls; image.functionStart folds it into SaveWriteValue, which ends at 0x679B20, so it is a separate function the walker runs past. 0xC89B0 and 0xC83E0 are the lookups a caller uses to get a token id at run time. The 0x678040-0x679640 run is the rest of this family - 22 more free save-writing helpers between SaveWriteToken's neighbours and SaveBeginBlock, each with its own register convention, and naming them finishes the save side.
